title: Blog
lead: Publish structured articles with editorial authors, topic archives, scheduled releases and moderated discussion.

sections.title: Prepare authors and topics
steps: Open Blog → Taxonomies and choose authors, categories or tags. Create a clear display name for each needed entry.
For example, create an editorial author and a “News” category. Edit existing entries instead of creating near-duplicates.
Remove an entry only after checking articles that use it; catalog revisions are available in History.

sections.title: Create and edit an article
steps: Open Blog → Overview and choose New article. Enter its slug, title, excerpt and author, then select categories and tags.
Compose structured blocks or select HTML/Mustache explicitly. The shared Visual/Code editor handles authored HTML; switching format does not convert the old blocks automatically.

Choose existing public images through the media selector or enter an allowed remote URL. Upload new media in Images first and provide alternative text. Set individual SEO/social metadata where needed.

Template shows the active theme and its Blog layout. Alternate post formats depend on declared template support; the editor does not invent executable template paths. History and Trash remain available for revision and recovery.

sections.title: Preview, publish and schedule
steps: Select Pending review when an article is ready for editorial review. It remains unavailable publicly until explicitly published. Use Featured article to pin it above ordinary items in the default article listing.
Save a draft and open its authenticated preview. Check headings, links, images and the active template before publishing.
Set the publication state and UTC release time. A published article with a future release time stays unavailable publicly until it is due.
Review the public article, list, RSS and sitemap once released. Unpublished or removed content is excluded from these public projections.

sections.title: Raw articles and authored Mustache blocks
steps: blog:posts(limit:1–12, category: optional category ID) returns items: id, title, excerpt, href, image, publishedAt, author (display name), categories and tags (arrays of display names). Only released published articles are included. blog:latest remains available for existing template-owned card formats.

Add an HTML / Mustache block to an article to reuse the core authoring control and public data bindings. Example with alias news: {{#news.items}}
{{title}}

{{excerpt}}

{{/news.items}}{{^news.items}}

No articles yet.

{{/news.items}}. Never add a service that recursively renders the same document. Blog is also a Homepage source for published article bodies; comments, moderation details, credentials and the site frame are excluded.

sections.title: Insert Blog data in other layouts
steps: In a compatible HTML/Mustache editor, bind blog:posts as news, limit 3 and optionally a category ID. Use the preceding example to render escaped data.
For older template-owned components, select blog:latest with a supported format, such as cards. The template owns that format’s HTML/CSS.
In Homepage source mode, choose a published Blog article to reuse its body. Private comments, moderation and the article’s surrounding site frame are excluded.

sections.title: Configure and moderate discussion
steps: Open Blog → Settings to review publication defaults and discussion options. Comments start disabled; enable them only when discussion is intended.

In an article editor, use Allow comments on this article to open or close submissions. Global discussion must also be enabled. Closing an article keeps its approved comments visible and rejects new submissions, including an already-open form.
Open Comments and inspect pending entries. Approve a suitable comment, keep it pending, mark spam or remove it using the available actions.
Only approved eligible comments are public. Submissions contain no email/IP fields; exports omit comments and moderation records.

sections.title: Restore articles and revisions
steps: Open History and inspect the revision before restoring the catalog. Resolve concurrent edit conflicts by reloading and reconciling the current version.
Move an unwanted article to Trash, then open the final Trash item to recover it when needed. Review its publication state after recovery.
Keep content backups as part of site operations; history and trash are private and are not included in initial production exports.
